content:
I'm starting to PR some results about subobject classifiers and elementary topoi, and in the startup i thought i'd be nice to do some small cleaning of the current mathlib design... Before i start PRing my ideas for cleaning this up, i thought i'd be good to check that i'm not an idiot and these are sensible, so i'd like to get some opinions on the following:

  • we should move docs#Classifier and docs#HasClassifier into the Subobject namespace (to avoid later confusion with partial map classifiers)
  • we should move the file CategoryTheory/Topos/Classifier.lean to the CategoryTheory/Subobject/ folder, probably even a new CategoryTheory/Subobject/Classifier/ folder and rename the file to Defs.lean or somesuch, as i have a bunch of files which would also fit in such a folder.

Additionally, i'm not sure what the correct order to go about this is, especially concerning deprecating, so i also appreciate some advice/instruction in that direction.

if people want to know what kind of thing i'm planning to PR regarding toposes, eventually i hope to PR my (formalization of a) proof of the fundamental theorem of topos theory (over categories of a topos are toposes), which will in particular give us a proof that sheaf categories (of types) are locally cartesian closed (as well as a concrete construction of exponentials in those over categories)

I think your first two bullets are very sensible. I'm not completely certain which proof of the fundamental theorem is the one which is right for mathlib (as we discussed elsewhere, there are (at least) two ways of doing this), but I'm sure that many of your prereqs will be useful regardless.

i have to say i'm not completely convinced Subobject.HasClassifier will be a better name though, as it would suggest it's some subobject that has a classifier, rather than the category having a classifier of subobjects... does anyone have a better suggestion?

My own preference is CategoryTheory.HasSubobjectClassifier for this. Classifiers for partial maps and other gadgets can just be CategoryTheory.HasGadgetClassifier. Like you said, I would also have not confidently guessed what CategoryTheory.HasClassifier or Subobject.HasClassifier is.
The restructuring of the files/folders seem sensible to me too.
